precepts.label: Nehemiah 2:10
precepts.why:
The Lord has set watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem “which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. Watchmen pay attention to the condition of the people and to the enemy coming to destroy the people. “ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.”

Nehemiah shows how the enemy takes it when Israel speaks up: “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” They do not like it when we speak up for our people.

That is why our enemies want us silent, locked away with the key thrown away and our mouths zipped. They call us troublemakers. Yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. They want a quiet slave.

The squeaky wheel gets the oil. Quiet people are ignored, and noisy people force others to take action. So we will complain, judge, bring out the records and tell it like it is, and we will beg the Lord and give him no rest, like the widow before the unjust judge, until he kills our enemies and sets Jerusalem up on high.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 17:12
precepts.why:
“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” Succours means comforts. Fear is a betraying comfort.

We are encouraged to be sports figures, entertainers and dancers, to frolic: to play, jump and move about in a happy, lively, carefree way, and never think about anything serious, because then we become a danger. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false. The athlete makes millions running up and down the court and thinks he has made it, but the real soul of him knows he is still a slave. Keeping us in the silly mode makes us consumers, not people who run our own banks and medical centers.

Kaepernick caught the fever. He looked at what was happening to his people while he was up there throwing the ball, got serious and stood up, and you saw how they dealt with him. His teammates know he did the right thing, but they have to pretend they are all right. That pretending is the fear: they stay in that mess and never stand up to be men, lying to themselves that they are comfortable being clowns.

So the watchmen of Isaiah 62 cannot hold their peace. We cannot drown out the horrible squeaking of our wretched condition, the psychological traumas we live through, with frolic, drugs, alcohol or music. We cannot be dancing slaves made to look whole while inside there is a spiritual rot we can no longer afford. We must stand up and be real men and women, keep not silence, and give the Lord no rest.

precepts.label: Romans 7:15
precepts.why:
The foundational question is: am I who I was created to be, or am I what I was conditioned to become? It is not a surface-level question; it is an identity question that deals with the real soul of man and woman. Everything about us, our patterns, our responses, our beliefs, our defenses, has been shaped by one of two forces: creation or conditioning. Creation speaks to design; conditioning speaks to experience. One is intentional, the other reactive. One reflects origin, the image God made; the other reflects adaptation, to slavery, to ghettos, to being taken advantage of, to being unclean, a gang member, a drug addict. That is not who we really are, and most people live somewhere in between without ever telling the two apart.

Paul shows that fight in Romans 7:15: “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” What he ends up doing, the real him does not allow. What his spirit would do, the conditioned self will not follow. And what the real him hates, the righteous part connected to God that hates evil, he does anyway, acting from conditioning and not from what the Lord made him to be. “If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That duality goes on with us every day.

Christ said you must deny yourself. The you that does the denying is the part God is dealing with; the self is the composite of the conditioning you were made into. So examine your own thoughts and behaviors and ask: why am I behaving like this? Is this the real me, or a response to what I have been conditioned to be?

Most of the time when we deal with our people, we are dealing with the mask, the representative, like the man holding up a sign in front of himself. The real soul is buried and scared, hiding under a tarp of trauma, lies, deceit and psychological hang-ups. The greatness buried under self-doubt has not surfaced yet. That is what is meant by the Negro being made in a lab: the real him has not stood up. We have to encourage that real spirit to come forward and be the image God made.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:27-28
precepts.why:
You were created with intention: not randomly formed, not accidentally designed, not undefined in purpose. You have a purpose; you just lost your way. “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” Replenish the earth means have babies.

This is the original declaration, not only about humanity in general but about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman. Not the whore, the drug addict, the drug dealer they told you that you are. The real you is about righteousness, and you cannot define yourself by the conditioning of how you have been made to look. Conditioning says, we want to make a slave out of him, out of her, and make them think that is what they innately are. That is the point of saying the Negro was created in a lab: the real him has not stood up yet, the real us has not even surfaced yet.

You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction. Not the image of your traumatic experiences, even though we have been through all kinds of trauma. Not the image crafted by an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth back to you. Where it was said that we are not his people, it shall be said that we are the sons and daughters of God. We are not what they say we are; we are what God said we are. Carry yourselves that way and teach it to your children, because this world will turn them upside down if you are not serious about it.

Before conditioning entered, before survival strategies developed, before the false self was built, there was an image, an original design, and that design carries attributes: the capacity for creativity, for dominion, the capacity to rule, and for fruitfulness, children and nationhood. These are not just aspirations, like a novel we read. They are original; they are in our DNA, placed in us before the world opened its lips to say anything. When people see what we build and say it must be a sellout, that is a dysfunctional mind that believes we can't do anything. Men and women, whatever you went through, you can fix it. In IUIC we told everyone who said we couldn't to go to hell, and we did what we had to do.

precepts.label: Exodus 11:7
precepts.why:
The attributes of the image were placed in us before the world had its say, and Exodus 11:7 shows how God guards his people: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Are we the children of Israel? Then not a dog shall open its lips against us. No one can talk against us or anything that belongs to us. The Lord put a difference so that the world may know. We are his holy jewels, the jewellery God will wear around his neck, the apple of his eye. When they speak against us, they are speaking against his jewels and his people.

Carry yourselves like that, and never mind people who say you can't boast. Even in captivity: it is only temporary. We are not the finished product of what they did to us. A day is coming when this will be gone, and everything that ever spoke against our people will face judgment. They say, you don't talk like a slave. That is because we are not slaves.

Be like Christ. On the cross, he knew he could call down legions to wipe them out in the blink of an eye, because he already had the power, and he says we will be joint heirs with him. The world is scared to death that we will ever make that connection. They do not want us connected to that kind of power.

precepts.label: Isaiah 43:21
precepts.why:
“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” This people is the Israelites, Judah: God formed us for himself, to show forth his praise, and all the other nations will catch hell.

Put that in your spirit and put it in your children's spirit. Teach your children they are superior, because they are. The world tells us lies: it shows us Superman and Batman and all kinds of fools on TV and makes us think we are nothing but criminals. Then, when we say the reverse, they try the Jedi mind trick and make us think we are doing something wrong. That is why sons need fathers in the household who think this way, so they grow up in the right posture.

We were not formed for survival or to be a product of our environment. We were formed for a purpose that comes from outside our circumstances, connected to the nature and intent of the Most High who formed us. That is Jeremiah 1:5: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Before the sperm hit the egg, we already existed and were known by him, and he chose which spirit to send, this one rather than that one, for a purpose. “and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations”: whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be. He made us the children of Israel and put talents in us. That is why those talents must be organized and not wasted. Don't bring self-doubt; get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

precepts.label: Revelation 6:5-6
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the prince of Tyrus got his riches “By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick”. Traffic means trade. Revelation 6 shows the same man and how he runs the trade of the world: “And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third beast say, Come and see.” This third beast, this powerful angel, says to John, I am going to show you something.

“And I beheld, and lo a black horse”. The black horse represents the dark nations that Esau is over. This whole chapter deals with Esau's rulership, from the white horse to the red horse, and now the black horse. “and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand”: the white man sitting on the black horse, holding a pair of balances, a scale of right and wrong weight and measure.

“A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny”. Who dictates how much wheat should cost worldwide? It is America: their World Bank, their IMF. They control the economy of the world. They are the ones that say Jamaica's money is no good, Sierra Leone's money is no good, Haiti's money is garbage. Yet those countries have all the resources, and America doesn't. But might makes right: America has the military arsenal, so all nations have to shut the hell up. “and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine”: see thou, meaning do not deal unjustly.

So verses 5 and 6 are the IMF and the World Bank, the world economy. That is the “great wisdom” and “traffick” of Ezekiel 28 by which the prince increased his riches and lifted up his heart. And don't let America tell you it is broke: its debt is in its own money, and it prints its own money. How can you owe yourself?

precepts.label: Matthew 16:26
precepts.why:
The prince of Tyrus has “gotten gold and silver into thy treasures”, and our people try to get involved in America's wealth, America's riches. They want a piece of the pie. But getting a piece of America's pie is dangerous. Christ asks the question: “For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?”

In order to get the fame and fortune that many of our people so desperately want, because we want to take care of our friends and family, you have to sell your soul. You must give your soul to these people.

That is often called hush money. Someone as wealthy as LeBron James takes care of his friends, which is admirable, and his family, which is admirable. But in terms of helping his people on a major level, he is not allowed to do that. That is hush money: hush the F up, and just take care of your friends and family. Oprah, all these people; many of them have gone to Epstein's Island, and their names are on the list.

So the riches of the man who says “I am a God” are not a blessing to reach for. Whoever gains his world gets it by trading away his soul, and the Lord has already said he will bring the terrible of the nations upon that man and bring him down to the pit.

precepts.label: Daniel 2:44
precepts.why:
Daniel 7:27 says “the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom”. That is why Daniel 2:44 says the same: “And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed”.

The days of these kings are the same kings of Daniel 7, the thrones cast down in Armageddon when Christ comes back to smash and destroy and set his people up in rulership. The kingdom the God of heaven sets up is you, sisters and brothers, the nation of Israel, and it is starting now. A lot of people don't like that, but the Most High is building this kingdom right now, in the age of their decadence.

“and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms”. The Most High's kingdom, the nation of Israel with Christ and the Most High and the angels leading us, shall break the nations and make them bend to the will of God, or death. Everybody is going to be made to follow the words of this Bible, its laws and commandments. Full stop.

“and it shall stand for ever.” That is the everlasting kingdom of Daniel 7:27. Remember these words: the kingdom the Lord is setting up shall stand for ever, and we are supposed to be in the image of understanding that, not the image of dysfunction. All the wealth of the nations under the whole heaven, the whole planet, has to be given back to Israel, including the nations themselves.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

The place where it was said, ye are not my people, is the place where we were made to be dysfunctional, where we were made a mess, where they called us coon and spear-chucker. They called us everything except the Israelites. In that very place the Most High is going to beautify the meek with salvation, and there it shall be said, ye are the sons of the living God. That is Daniel 7:27: the kingdom under the whole heaven given “to the people of the saints of the most High”.

The Lord is going to punish the nations for what they called us and did to us, because we are God's heritage. Those who put their nasty, mangy hands on us touched the apple of his eye, and they are going to pay for it. Our brothers and sisters were hung and suffered all kinds of evil, and the Most High has the chart on everything. The Lord allowed it to happen, and he is still going to make them pay for doing it.

precepts.label: Romans 9:17-21
precepts.why:
The Lord allows the nations to afflict us and still makes them pay, and who can resist his will? That is the argument of Romans 9. “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” The same purpose for which God raised up Pharaoh is the purpose for which he is raising up Esau: to show his power by channeling his destructive anger through him, and to get his glory by destroying the man everybody is worshipping, so they will all know the Most High is the real power.

“Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.” He raised up Pharaoh to resist God, and he makes Esau do the same. He is fattening Esau up with weapons, technology, power and pride, the way you fatten a turkey before one of their wicked holidays, and then he will cut him down.

“Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?” How can he find fault with the man when he gave him all the weapons and made him resist? Esau cannot resist the will of God, and neither could Pharaoh. Pharaoh wanted to let the Israelites go, and the Lord hardened his heart.

“Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Esau was formed as the fitting vessel for God's destruction; one vessel is for wine and one is for the bowels.

So you had better be glad you are the Israelites. After slavery, Jim Crow and the lynchings, to die with the same man who did it to you would be crazy. The kingdom goes to the saints of the Most High, and the vessel of dishonour is broken.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:1-4
precepts.why:
Habakkuk describes the man who “transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man”. The wine he transgresses by is his Christianity and his democracy, which are virtually the same thing: his policies, his religions, his politics. Obadiah names the proud man: “Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”.

“We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.” Someone is going to rise up among the nations and say, let's go against America, let's go against Israel in battle. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.”

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high”. Edom is the prideful man. They come from the Caucasus Mountains and dwelt in the clefts of the rock through the Middle Ages; in Obadiah's time it was the place called Petra today, and look at the architecture, just like Rome, just like Washington D.C. Their high habitation now is their skyscrapers. “That saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” To say that you have to have power: they are saying nobody can beat us.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. Their symbol is the eagle: take out your dollar bill. Who is sending satellites and doing space travel? America. So Edom is not the Arabs: the Arabs are not doing space travel, and their symbol is not the eagle. Nor is it the American Indian, who uses the eagle, because if they had had power they would have blown the white man off the face of the earth. People throw these things out to confuse the new converts.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” That began when the truth started to come out in the 1960s. And Habakkuk shows how: he “neither keepeth at home”, a busybody in every nation, destabilising country after country by economic or conventional war and gathering the residue of those peoples to America and England. “Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee”: terrorism from within, slowly but surely, “Because thou hast spoiled many nations”.

precepts.label: Romans 8:13-14
precepts.why:
It is not a sin to drink. But when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation; it is not to be used in that manner. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome these things.

“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die”. To live after the flesh is to obey the elements of the flesh: going to the bottle and making that the outlet. The end of that road is always death, just as Habakkuk 2:12 shows that there is always an evil road, and at the end of it you find death.

“but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live”. That is where we are. The drinking problem in this land is a quarter trillion dollars, but the commandments fix all of that.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” That is how we are to be. So we should not be overcome with that evil; we have to overcome that evil with good, and the good is God's laws.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 31:28-29
precepts.why:
“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind”. Measurably. The wine is not the sin; the measure is the key. “But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind”. That is the key point: bitterness of the mind.

The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element on the earth was created by the Lord, and it has its function and its purpose. But if you use it and abuse it, you cannot be useful for the nation.

It is the same with alcoholism as it is with food, which the Bishop has been bringing out: all of it has a balance, and if you overuse it you fall. Our oppressors are depending on us to lose that balance. That is why you have the KFCs across the street from Domino's, and the liquor stores in our neighborhoods: they are depending on you to fall into that destruction, that chaos, that confusion.

Nobody out there is drinking measurably or sociably; it is used to drown out reality, and it will kill you. So overcoming evil with good means holding the balance the Most High set in every element, and not letting the bottle become the outlet.

precepts.label: Galatians 2:4
precepts.why:
“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”. It is not another because it is found in the law of Moses. “but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” They are the same men of Acts 15, who went out from us and troubled the churches. Paul says, if any man preach any other gospel, “let him be accursed”. Those men were running around joining the churches and causing confusion by infiltration, pushing a gospel we are no longer under: going back to sacrificing animals. That is another gospel.

Chapter 2 names them: “And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage”. The liberty we have is that we no longer offer up animals. Christ died on the cross, and we are free from that burden. The bondage they wanted to bring us into was sacrificing animals again to be saved, like Acts 15.

So Galatians 5 says “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.” If animal sacrifice saves you, Christ died for nothing and you are fallen from grace. Yet “ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh”: do not use this freedom to do what you want and sin.

Likewise today, Christians will come in here and do the same thing: accept the identity, but not the theology, using the same book and the same Bible to push Christianity. That is the same infiltration in reverse. As John says, “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and those who trouble you shall bear their judgment.

precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:1-3
precepts.why:
Paul told Timothy he was persuaded that Christ “is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.” Paul committed his soul, his life, to Christ. What day? Thessalonians explains it: “Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That day is the second coming, and all twelve tribes can only gather unto Christ.

“That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” People were writing letters in Paul’s name saying the second coming had already happened and you missed it. Paul said, I don’t care if you got a letter signed by me, I didn’t write that; that day did not happen yet. Remember in the sixties the FBI would write letters to the Black Panthers and other black organizations in each other’s names. They were doing the same thing with Paul.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” Christ is not going to return until all twelve tribes fall away into captivity. Christians break that down as people leaving Christianity; it is not talking about that crap. It is falling into captivity, as Luke 21:24 says: “they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” All twelve shall fall, and we are still living in the times of the Gentiles.

In Paul’s day, Judah, Benjamin and Levi had not fallen completely; they were still in the land. But 70 AD was soon approaching. So the day Paul committed his soul against has not come yet, and it could not come until all of us fell. And we all fell.

precepts.label: Joel 2:31
precepts.why:
“That day” in Paul’s words to Timothy is the second coming, and Joel shows what kind of day it is: “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” This is a time of war and devastation. When Christ returns, it is going to be a great and terrible day.

Amos says the same: “Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.” We say we can’t wait for the day of the Lord because we don’t really comprehend the magnitude of what is going to happen. You think it is going to be a bright day and Christ will take us all up to the kingdom. It is not that type of a day; it is not that type of a party.

Zephaniah: “The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress.” Don’t think that when the Lord returns we are all going to be standing and cheering. We are going to be running and weeping.

Christ said it in Matthew 24: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days”, which is Jacob’s trouble, “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, because the sky will be black, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles dropping from the sky. The powers of the nations shall be shaken with war. “and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” You think you will be happy, stomping your feet and clapping; the Bible says all the tribes shall mourn, meaning cry bitterly. That is the day Paul was preparing Timothy for, and why he told him to stir up the gift, not fear, and not be ashamed of the afflictions of the gospel.

precepts.label: Mark 4:16-19
precepts.why:
“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world.” Demas traveled with Paul and warred with Paul, and he forsook Paul. He saw the looseness of the women: Paul, I’ve got to go, my man, I can’t roll with you no more, I got needs. He let that overcome him. Crescens left for Galatia, Titus for Dalmatia. Mark shows what happened to Paul’s companions, men who were strong in the Lord and in the power of his might. Those guys are some of you guys.

“And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness.” I’m an Israelite, we got history, oh I love it. “And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time.” No root: I don’t study, I don’t addict myself to the ministry, I like my sports, I like my porn, the Bible comes last. So you only endure this gospel for a time.

“afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.” Offended, and you leave. Affliction is things that happen to you; persecution is what happens to you for the word’s sake, because you stand strong in this Bible. That is why Paul told Timothy not to be ashamed of his affliction, to suffer in it with him and stir up the gift within him. Christ lets us know some of us are going to leave this truth because of affliction.

And Satan will test. He asks the Lord, can I test him? Can I test her? The brother with a proclivity for the male gender went to the gym at two in the morning, where the freaks come out at night, found two men in the shower, stood there five whole minutes, and they invited him to join in. If you are struggling, stay out of the gym; do calisthenics at your house. You are trying to fight a spirit; don’t go around spirits like that.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, a piece of the American pie, may not be your thing. But the lust of other things is anything in you that nobody else knows. You may hide it very well, but God knows it is there, Satan knows it is there, and you do too. Satan is not tempting you with a pork chop. He looks into your soul, sees what you are battling with, and asks to tempt you right there.

That is what took Demas, Crescens and Titus, and it is what Paul went through with Alexander the coppersmith, who was in the ministry and turned against it, “for he hath greatly withstood our words.” We have seen the same: men in the gospel who went online to try to tear this down. “At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me.” Christ already prophesied it: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers and sisters we broke bread with, who stayed in our homes and knew our families, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight. God is not going to bless your hands after you did so much evil to your brothers and sisters.

The Lord is “not willing that any should perish”, so any one of us that comes into this truth, the desire is for you to make it. Peter says “give diligence to make your calling and election sure”. The Most High called you sisters and you brothers in here, and that was not a waste. It was made to happen in the heavens when it was time for you to wake up. Just as there was a conversation in the heavens about Job, when Satan wanted to tempt him, there were conversations about you repenting. That's some love right there. Understand that sacred calling.

Then Sirach: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” He wants to try you to make sure you are fit for the kingdom. But he first selected you. He brought you into his marvellous gospel to wake you up and bring you up as princes and princesses; no longer are you to be on the dunghill. As you prepare your soul for temptation, that is the Lord trying you to make sure you are worthy of that calling.

It was already discussed in the heavens to bring you in, so it is up to us to stay diligent and steadfast, and not get pulled off by evil, wickedness, sin, temptations and the things our people get caught up in. We are a chosen vessel, and you have to see yourselves that way.

Peter goes on, “for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”: that is the guarantee of keeping God's commandments. So why squander the chance Christ died to give you because of some bad habits and temptations? Every one of your spirits is precious to the Most High, and it hurts leadership to see you get weak and lose the faith. A mind is a terrible thing to waste. Many brothers and sisters came in with good gifts, got weak hearted, went back out, and are doing nothing. This was the time to shine.

precepts.why:
“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more”. The merchants are the corporations that make major deals with countries. The gold, silver and precious stones come this way by ship in those big containers, and the majority of what is listed comes from the continent of Africa. Then: “and slaves”: that was you and me. “And souls of men”: you want a piece of the pie, you have to sell your soul. There are things you must do.

Ecclesiasticus says it: “Why is earth and ashes proud?” Earth and ashes represents man; why is man proud? “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man”. They covet what does not belong to them. If you are covetous, you want a piece of the American pie, those billions of dollars in contracts. “For such an one setteth his own soul to sale; because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels.” While he lives he casts away his bowels, the lower intestine, the rectum.

You think Oprah got all that money just because she was a great talk show host? You think LeBron and these athletes got those contracts because nobody is as good as them? Michael Jai White is a good actor, but there are certain things he said he is not going to do, so he does not get those contracts. Ye said, if you see a video of me with a goat, because he knew what they held over him. They have something on all of them. The model from our Houston school, the Black Starlet who found a line of producers at the door: to get the contract you cast away your bowels.

That is why Paul says “they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” Covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, and it starts in the mind; covet and you will steal, steal and you will lie, and it goes on to murder. The fear that keeps them from repenting is being publicly humiliated for what they did to get their fortunes, the way they destroyed Wendy Williams. But the Lord can still preserve the soul: come out of that lifestyle.

precepts.label: Judges 3:1-2
precepts.why:
Ezra saw the city of the kingdom with its narrow entrance, “like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”. That fire and deep water is the nations afflicting us. Judges makes the point about the nations: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan”.

He didn't get rid of all the nations. He said, no, I'm going to leave something there, because I don't want you to just skate through. You have to learn some things. If we did not have to be buffeted by our enemies, our journey would be quite smooth; but God put it that way because we messed up, and now we have to serve them, and they are going to make it hell for us to get the kingdom.

“Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof”. We didn't know about war before; now we know about war. We are getting the training now. When we get into the kingdom we are going to be experts in everything, bad upon bad, because we will have done it all and endured it all. That is what is going to make us perfect.

Captivity and persecution are hard and rough; nobody wants to go through these things. They can kill the body, but they cannot kill the spirit. They can do all kind of evil to my body physically, but when I come back, I'm going to hang your ass. That is the mindset you have to have: going for the kingdom regardless of what is thrown at you, to persevere between the fire on one side and the deep water on the other. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

precepts.label: Psalms 83:1-4
precepts.why:
Achior runs Israel's whole history down to Holofernes, and in it is part of the key to getting out of this mess: “whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them.” So the objective of our enemies is to keep us from obeying God, to keep us in dysfunction so they can dominate us. They love that we're brilliant; they want the body and the mind, but they don't want us using that mind for ourselves. And the counsel he gives: “if there be any error against this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them.” That is exactly what is happening to us now. “But if there be no iniquity in their nation, let my lord now pass by, lest their Lord defend them.” That's where our power is: checking each other so there is no sin in the nation.

Add this to your prayers: “Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God. For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.” They are God's enemies, lifting up their heads against everything that is about the Most High.

“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” AIPAC counsel, The Israel Project counsel, ADL counsel, Canary Mission counsel: consultation, secret meetings against us. The nations are terrified that we are learning and teaching this Bible. An Israeli official came down to Atlanta, and in a meeting with AIPAC and the ADL they said the black man leading was the number one threat. Not Hamas, not Hezbollah: the blacks in this country, because they read the prophecy.

“They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” In their meetings, the discussion is to cut us off from the Most High, from who we truly are, from the image of God, and morph us into the image of dysfunction. They did it through a slave system designed to destroy the manhood of the black male, and they do it in the schools, killing the confidence of our sons by the fourth grade. They didn't bring dummies here: we were warriors and family heads, kings, princes, judges, architects, engineers, doctors, mathematicians, an industrious and skillful people. So no, we're not niggas; that lie garbage was given to us to make us think we are a different image than what God made us. They are not doing it to those over there. They do it to us because we are the Israelites.

precepts.label: Psalms 64:1-6
precepts.why:
“Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy. Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked; from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity.” It is the same secret counsel of Psalms 83, taken against the people who, as Achior told Holofernes, can only be overcome when they sin against their God.

“Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words.” Their bitter words: calling us anti-Semitic, when we are the Semites, from Shem, and their fathers came from Esau.

“That they may shoot in secret at the perfect: suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not. They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them? They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.” They think deep on how to trap us into perpetuating our own destruction: making us image ourselves as nothing, so they no longer have to enforce it. Parading a simple brother in a dress, stripping our women, keeping us clowns on the court and on the stage who know nothing of their ancestors.

That is the image of dysfunction they laid as a snare, so that there would be error in this people and it would be their ruin. The answer is to get back into the commandments so there is no iniquity in the nation, and the Lord defends us. If we as men do not do this work, no other species will.
